common.text: All reports describe failure at the final pay/Place Order step of checkout, never earlier in the flow.
Failure is amount-dependent: orders above roughly four figures fail while smaller orders on the same integration succeed.
Onset clusters in the afternoon of 2026-08-11: first report says failures began "about 2:15" and was filed 14:14Z; independent monitoring confirms 500s "since Tuesday afternoon."

Deploy d6 (payment-service, "Enable enhanced fraud screening for high-value transactions") shipped 2026-08-11T13:36Z, roughly 40 minutes before the first report, and its description names exactly the affected population.
The failing endpoint is POST /v2/transactions — returning 500s in one report and timing out at about 30 seconds in another.
Symptom spans at least four currencies (USD, EUR, JPY) and NA/EU/JP-facing merchants, so it is not region-locked.
Failures are still occurring on day four of the incident, with no self-reported recovery.
12 distinct customers reported independently within roughly 3 days, including two enterprise accounts sampled at about $240k and about $190k ACV.

varies.text: Two distinct failure shapes: fast failures (error page, HTTP 500, apparent decline) versus hangs (about 30-second timeout, endless spinner, white screen, "nothing happens").
Threshold is reported in different units per merchant: about €1,000+ (bookings), about $1,000+ (gym equipment), about ¥150,000+ (distributor), and five-figure B2B carts.
Some merchants describe the failure as a card decline rather than an error, though banks show no charge attempt.
One member ticket names no amount at all — its cluster membership is inferred from timing and stage-of-checkout only.
Some tickets are B2B/quantity-driven (40+ seat licenses, quarterly restocks) rather than single high-priced items, but still cross the value threshold.
Reporting fidelity varies widely: monitoring/console-level detail in some tickets versus phone-call anecdotes in others.

ruled_out.text: Browser, device or client platform: failures reproduce on Chrome and Edge, on Safari/iPhone and Firefox, and on Chrome and Safari.
Single-customer misconfiguration: 12 distinct merchants across multiple currency regions with no shared integration pattern, and one explicitly states nothing changed on their side.
Genuine bank/issuer declines: banks show no charge attempt at all, so the failure happens before the card network is reached.

Pre-existing/long-standing defect: history search returned no archived checkout-failure tickets; the archived checkout hits were a gift-message how-to, an expired discount code, and a rate-limit question, all resolved as non-defects.

Deploy d5 (web-storefront seasonal theme/CSS refresh, 2026-08-09T11:20Z) as prime suspect: it shipped about 2 days earlier with no reports in the interim and is a presentation-layer change that cannot explain server-side 500s on POST /v2/transactions or amount-dependent behaviour.
Analytics/reporting timeouts surfaced by the same history search are outside this cluster (different surface, not checkout) and were not investigated.

hypotheses.text: Deploy d6's enhanced fraud screening added a synchronous screening call on the high-value path, and that call errors or hangs — which would explain both the 500s and the ~30-second timeouts appearing only above the value threshold, starting ~40 minutes after the deploy.
hypotheses.not_examined: No access to payment-service code, deploy diff, logs, or the trace attached to t228; the screening vendor's latency/error rate and any timeout configuration were not examined, and no deploys after 2026-08-11T15:00Z were queried.

hypotheses.text: The threshold appears to be applied after FX conversion at roughly 1,000 USD-equivalent, since the JPY boundary is about ¥150,000 (~$1,000) rather than a raw numeric 1,000 — suggesting a single currency-agnostic converted-amount rule rather than per-currency limits.
hypotheses.not_examined: No access to the screening threshold configuration, FX conversion logic, or per-request amount logs; exact pass/fail boundary values per merchant were not confirmed beyond what tickets state.

hypotheses.text: The two failure shapes may be one mechanism at different latencies (fast reject vs. gateway/browser timeout) rather than two bugs — fast errors and hangs are reported by different merchants but never in a way that separates them by amount or region.
hypotheses.not_examined: No server-side latency distribution, gateway timeout settings, or error-code breakdown were available; whether hung requests eventually create charges or orphaned transactions was not checked.

hypotheses.text: Some hung requests may leave shoppers uncertain whether they were charged, since at least one merchant's customers interpreted the failure as a decline — a possible double-charge/orphan-transaction exposure worth checking alongside the primary fix.
hypotheses.not_examined: No transaction-ledger or reconciliation data was reviewed; no confirmation of whether any authorization was created for failed attempts.
